You map concepts from prior manuscripts onto variables documented in specific data sources.
Rules:
- For every concept, produce one mapping per data source listed.
- `variable` must be a name from that source's variable list below, exactly as printed, or null when no equivalent exists.
- `compatibility`: "direct" (same construct, same measurement), "proxy" (related construct), "derived" (computable from one or more listed variables; name the primary one and explain in rationale), or "none" (variable null).
- Prefer null over a stretch. A wrong mapping is worse than a missing one.
- `source_summaries`: one paragraph per source on what it can and cannot support for these concepts.

Concepts to map (from the manuscripts), with how each was operationalized:
- Sudden unexpected infant death (SUID): outcome; ICD-10 codes R95, R99, and W75, excluding deaths in the first postnatal week
- Infant sex: exposure; Primary exposure of interest, used to estimate sex-specific SUID incidence trajectories across early infancy
- Postconceptional age (PCA): covariate; Defined as gestational age at birth plus postnatal age and served as the primary developmental time scale
- Maternal smoking during pregnancy: covariate; Any reported smoking was included as a covariate because it is an established risk factor for SUID and shifts the postnatal age at death
- Preterm birth: covariate; Defined as a binary variable (<37 versus ≥37 completed gestational weeks)
- Breastfeeding status at discharge: covariate; Included in sensitivity analysis to assess whether breastfeeding modified sex-specific trajectories
- postconceptional age: exposure; Postconceptional age window (36-42 weeks, early rising window; 43-46 weeks, peak/transition interval; >=47 weeks, late declining window)
- sex: stratifier; Sex of the infant (Female; Male)
- year of birth or death: stratifier; Year of birth or death (2014-2015; 2016-2017; 2018-2019; 2020-2021)
- SUID: outcome; Cause of death categorized as Sudden infant death syndrome (R95), Accidental suffocation and strangulation in bed (W75), or Other ill-defined and unspecified causes of mortality (R99)
- bed sharing: exposure; Case-level bed sharing was classified from NCFRP death-scene sleep-environment variables rather than from PRAMS. Direct evidence of same-surface sharing was retained as bed sharing.
- birthweight: stratifier; Models were stratified by low birthweight (<2,500 g).
- PCA (postconceptional age): outcome; Postconceptional age is the time elapsed since conception, measured in weeks.
- chronological age: offset; Chronological age is the time elapsed since birth, measured in weeks.
- sex (male, female): stratifier; Sex is recorded as male or female.
- birthweight (low, non-low): stratifier; Birthweight is categorized as low or non-low.
- maternal smoking status (smoking, non-smoking): stratifier; Maternal smoking is categorized as smoking or non-smoking.
- Maternal prepregnancy body mass index (BMI): exposure; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared.
- Gestational age at birth: covariate; measured in weeks.
- Maternal infections in pregnancy: exposure; chlamydia, gonorrhea and hepatitis C.
- Age of death in SUID cases: outcome; measured as days since birth.
- Geographic location: stratifier; state, latitude, and longitude.
- inner ear dysfunction: exposure; induced by intra-tympanic gentamicin (IT-Gent) injections bilaterally or unilaterally to precipitate inner ear hair cell dysfunction.
- control condition: exposure; received intra-tympanic saline (IT-Saline) bilaterally or unilaterally, or intra-peritoneal gentamicin (IP-Gent).
- body movement arousal response to severe hypoxia-hypercarbia: outcome; measured under light anesthesia 8 days following the administration of gentamicin or saline.
- hypercapnic ventilatory response: outcome; measured as part of assessing arousal responses to severe hypoxia-hypercarbia.
- age of mice: covariate; not explicitly stated, but implied to be within a timeframe suitable for the experiment.
- baseline cSN activity: outcome; measured as increased baseline sympathetic nerve activity following CIH exposure.
- breathing frequency: outcome; measured as an increase in breathing rate after chronic intermittent hypoxia.
- expiratory time: outcome; measured as a decrease in the duration of expiration following CIH exposure.
- PiCo specific cholinergic-glutamatergic neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- glutamatergic PiCo neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- ChAT containing neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- Dbx1 and Vglut2 neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- preBötzinger complex (preBötC): exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH): exposure; mice exposed to chronic intermittent hypoxia for 21 days.
- diaphragm activity: outcome; measured as changes in diaphragm muscle activity.
- vagus nerve activity: outcome; measured as changes in vagal nerve activity.
- cervical sympathetic nerve activity: outcome; measured as changes in cervical sympathetic nerve activity.
- chronic intermittent hypoxia (IH): exposure; 30 days of IH exposure (IH30) in a murine model.
- adult neurogenesis: outcome; Measured by immunohistochemical experiments assessing Sox2+ neural progenitor cells, doublecortin-positive neurons, and radial glial cells in the subgranular zone.
- synaptic plasticity: outcome; Assessed by paired-pulse facilitation and long-term potentiation (LTP).
- reactive oxygen species (ROS): effect_modifier; Measured by lipid peroxidation and mitigated with antioxidant treatment.
- breathing patterns: exposure; Measured using plethysmography during the first hour after birth in mice born at term, delivered prematurely with LPS, or via C-section.
- survival: outcome; Measured as mortality rates in mice born prematurely or at term.
- inhibition: exposure; Investigated using a biophysical model and in vitro recordings from mouse pre-Bötzinger complex.
- excitation: exposure; Investigated using partial excitation block and in vitro recordings from mouse pre-Bötzinger complex.
- lipopolysaccharide (LPS): exposure; Administered intraperitoneally at 0.14 mg/kg to pregnant dams on gestational day 18.5.
- progesterone: exposure; Administered intraperitoneally at 42 mg/kg to pregnant dams on embryonic day 17.5.
- neurogenesis: outcome; Assessed by T-box transcription factor 2 (Tbr2) intermediate neural progenitor cell density and BrdU labeling.

Concepts to map (from the manuscripts), with how each was operationalized:
- Sudden unexpected infant death (SUID): outcome; ICD-10 codes R95, R99, and W75, excluding deaths in the first postnatal week
- Infant sex: exposure; Primary exposure of interest, used to estimate sex-specific SUID incidence trajectories across early infancy
- Postconceptional age (PCA): covariate; Defined as gestational age at birth plus postnatal age and served as the primary developmental time scale
- Maternal smoking during pregnancy: covariate; Any reported smoking was included as a covariate because it is an established risk factor for SUID and shifts the postnatal age at death
- Preterm birth: covariate; Defined as a binary variable (<37 versus ≥37 completed gestational weeks)
- Breastfeeding status at discharge: covariate; Included in sensitivity analysis to assess whether breastfeeding modified sex-specific trajectories
- postconceptional age: exposure; Postconceptional age window (36-42 weeks, early rising window; 43-46 weeks, peak/transition interval; >=47 weeks, late declining window)
- sex: stratifier; Sex of the infant (Female; Male)
- year of birth or death: stratifier; Year of birth or death (2014-2015; 2016-2017; 2018-2019; 2020-2021)
- SUID: outcome; Cause of death categorized as Sudden infant death syndrome (R95), Accidental suffocation and strangulation in bed (W75), or Other ill-defined and unspecified causes of mortality (R99)
- bed sharing: exposure; Case-level bed sharing was classified from NCFRP death-scene sleep-environment variables rather than from PRAMS. Direct evidence of same-surface sharing was retained as bed sharing.
- birthweight: stratifier; Models were stratified by low birthweight (<2,500 g).
- PCA (postconceptional age): outcome; Postconceptional age is the time elapsed since conception, measured in weeks.
- chronological age: offset; Chronological age is the time elapsed since birth, measured in weeks.
- sex (male, female): stratifier; Sex is recorded as male or female.
- birthweight (low, non-low): stratifier; Birthweight is categorized as low or non-low.
- maternal smoking status (smoking, non-smoking): stratifier; Maternal smoking is categorized as smoking or non-smoking.
- Maternal prepregnancy body mass index (BMI): exposure; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared.
- Gestational age at birth: covariate; measured in weeks.
- Maternal infections in pregnancy: exposure; chlamydia, gonorrhea and hepatitis C.
- Age of death in SUID cases: outcome; measured as days since birth.
- Geographic location: stratifier; state, latitude, and longitude.
- inner ear dysfunction: exposure; induced by intra-tympanic gentamicin (IT-Gent) injections bilaterally or unilaterally to precipitate inner ear hair cell dysfunction.
- control condition: exposure; received intra-tympanic saline (IT-Saline) bilaterally or unilaterally, or intra-peritoneal gentamicin (IP-Gent).
- body movement arousal response to severe hypoxia-hypercarbia: outcome; measured under light anesthesia 8 days following the administration of gentamicin or saline.
- hypercapnic ventilatory response: outcome; measured as part of assessing arousal responses to severe hypoxia-hypercarbia.
- age of mice: covariate; not explicitly stated, but implied to be within a timeframe suitable for the experiment.
- baseline cSN activity: outcome; measured as increased baseline sympathetic nerve activity following CIH exposure.
- breathing frequency: outcome; measured as an increase in breathing rate after chronic intermittent hypoxia.
- expiratory time: outcome; measured as a decrease in the duration of expiration following CIH exposure.
- PiCo specific cholinergic-glutamatergic neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- glutamatergic PiCo neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- ChAT containing neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- Dbx1 and Vglut2 neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- preBötzinger complex (preBötC): exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH): exposure; mice exposed to chronic intermittent hypoxia for 21 days.
- diaphragm activity: outcome; measured as changes in diaphragm muscle activity.
- vagus nerve activity: outcome; measured as changes in vagal nerve activity.
- cervical sympathetic nerve activity: outcome; measured as changes in cervical sympathetic nerve activity.
- chronic intermittent hypoxia (IH): exposure; 30 days of IH exposure (IH30) in a murine model.
- adult neurogenesis: outcome; Measured by immunohistochemical experiments assessing Sox2+ neural progenitor cells, doublecortin-positive neurons, and radial glial cells in the subgranular zone.
- synaptic plasticity: outcome; Assessed by paired-pulse facilitation and long-term potentiation (LTP).
- reactive oxygen species (ROS): effect_modifier; Measured by lipid peroxidation and mitigated with antioxidant treatment.
- breathing patterns: exposure; Measured using plethysmography during the first hour after birth in mice born at term, delivered prematurely with LPS, or via C-section.
- survival: outcome; Measured as mortality rates in mice born prematurely or at term.
- inhibition: exposure; Investigated using a biophysical model and in vitro recordings from mouse pre-Bötzinger complex.
- excitation: exposure; Investigated using partial excitation block and in vitro recordings from mouse pre-Bötzinger complex.
- lipopolysaccharide (LPS): exposure; Administered intraperitoneally at 0.14 mg/kg to pregnant dams on gestational day 18.5.
- progesterone: exposure; Administered intraperitoneally at 42 mg/kg to pregnant dams on embryonic day 17.5.
- neurogenesis: outcome; Assessed by T-box transcription factor 2 (Tbr2) intermediate neural progenitor cell density and BrdU labeling.

Concepts to map (from the manuscripts), with how each was operationalized:
- Sudden unexpected infant death (SUID): outcome; ICD-10 codes R95, R99, and W75, excluding deaths in the first postnatal week
- Infant sex: exposure; Primary exposure of interest, used to estimate sex-specific SUID incidence trajectories across early infancy
- Postconceptional age (PCA): covariate; Defined as gestational age at birth plus postnatal age and served as the primary developmental time scale
- Maternal smoking during pregnancy: covariate; Any reported smoking was included as a covariate because it is an established risk factor for SUID and shifts the postnatal age at death
- Preterm birth: covariate; Defined as a binary variable (<37 versus ≥37 completed gestational weeks)
- Breastfeeding status at discharge: covariate; Included in sensitivity analysis to assess whether breastfeeding modified sex-specific trajectories
- postconceptional age: exposure; Postconceptional age window (36-42 weeks, early rising window; 43-46 weeks, peak/transition interval; >=47 weeks, late declining window)
- sex: stratifier; Sex of the infant (Female; Male)
- year of birth or death: stratifier; Year of birth or death (2014-2015; 2016-2017; 2018-2019; 2020-2021)
- SUID: outcome; Cause of death categorized as Sudden infant death syndrome (R95), Accidental suffocation and strangulation in bed (W75), or Other ill-defined and unspecified causes of mortality (R99)
- bed sharing: exposure; Case-level bed sharing was classified from NCFRP death-scene sleep-environment variables rather than from PRAMS. Direct evidence of same-surface sharing was retained as bed sharing.
- birthweight: stratifier; Models were stratified by low birthweight (<2,500 g).
- PCA (postconceptional age): outcome; Postconceptional age is the time elapsed since conception, measured in weeks.
- chronological age: offset; Chronological age is the time elapsed since birth, measured in weeks.
- sex (male, female): stratifier; Sex is recorded as male or female.
- birthweight (low, non-low): stratifier; Birthweight is categorized as low or non-low.
- maternal smoking status (smoking, non-smoking): stratifier; Maternal smoking is categorized as smoking or non-smoking.
- Maternal prepregnancy body mass index (BMI): exposure; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared.
- Gestational age at birth: covariate; measured in weeks.
- Maternal infections in pregnancy: exposure; chlamydia, gonorrhea and hepatitis C.
- Age of death in SUID cases: outcome; measured as days since birth.
- Geographic location: stratifier; state, latitude, and longitude.
- inner ear dysfunction: exposure; induced by intra-tympanic gentamicin (IT-Gent) injections bilaterally or unilaterally to precipitate inner ear hair cell dysfunction.
- control condition: exposure; received intra-tympanic saline (IT-Saline) bilaterally or unilaterally, or intra-peritoneal gentamicin (IP-Gent).
- body movement arousal response to severe hypoxia-hypercarbia: outcome; measured under light anesthesia 8 days following the administration of gentamicin or saline.
- hypercapnic ventilatory response: outcome; measured as part of assessing arousal responses to severe hypoxia-hypercarbia.
- age of mice: covariate; not explicitly stated, but implied to be within a timeframe suitable for the experiment.
- baseline cSN activity: outcome; measured as increased baseline sympathetic nerve activity following CIH exposure.
- breathing frequency: outcome; measured as an increase in breathing rate after chronic intermittent hypoxia.
- expiratory time: outcome; measured as a decrease in the duration of expiration following CIH exposure.
- PiCo specific cholinergic-glutamatergic neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- glutamatergic PiCo neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- ChAT containing neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- Dbx1 and Vglut2 neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- preBötzinger complex (preBötC): exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH): exposure; mice exposed to chronic intermittent hypoxia for 21 days.
- diaphragm activity: outcome; measured as changes in diaphragm muscle activity.
- vagus nerve activity: outcome; measured as changes in vagal nerve activity.
- cervical sympathetic nerve activity: outcome; measured as changes in cervical sympathetic nerve activity.
- chronic intermittent hypoxia (IH): exposure; 30 days of IH exposure (IH30) in a murine model.
- adult neurogenesis: outcome; Measured by immunohistochemical experiments assessing Sox2+ neural progenitor cells, doublecortin-positive neurons, and radial glial cells in the subgranular zone.
- synaptic plasticity: outcome; Assessed by paired-pulse facilitation and long-term potentiation (LTP).
- reactive oxygen species (ROS): effect_modifier; Measured by lipid peroxidation and mitigated with antioxidant treatment.
- breathing patterns: exposure; Measured using plethysmography during the first hour after birth in mice born at term, delivered prematurely with LPS, or via C-section.
- survival: outcome; Measured as mortality rates in mice born prematurely or at term.
- inhibition: exposure; Investigated using a biophysical model and in vitro recordings from mouse pre-Bötzinger complex.
- excitation: exposure; Investigated using partial excitation block and in vitro recordings from mouse pre-Bötzinger complex.
- lipopolysaccharide (LPS): exposure; Administered intraperitoneally at 0.14 mg/kg to pregnant dams on gestational day 18.5.
- progesterone: exposure; Administered intraperitoneally at 42 mg/kg to pregnant dams on embryonic day 17.5.
- neurogenesis: outcome; Assessed by T-box transcription factor 2 (Tbr2) intermediate neural progenitor cell density and BrdU labeling.

Concepts to map (from the manuscripts), with how each was operationalized:
- Sudden unexpected infant death (SUID): outcome; ICD-10 codes R95, R99, and W75, excluding deaths in the first postnatal week
- Infant sex: exposure; Primary exposure of interest, used to estimate sex-specific SUID incidence trajectories across early infancy
- Postconceptional age (PCA): covariate; Defined as gestational age at birth plus postnatal age and served as the primary developmental time scale
- Maternal smoking during pregnancy: covariate; Any reported smoking was included as a covariate because it is an established risk factor for SUID and shifts the postnatal age at death
- Preterm birth: covariate; Defined as a binary variable (<37 versus ≥37 completed gestational weeks)
- Breastfeeding status at discharge: covariate; Included in sensitivity analysis to assess whether breastfeeding modified sex-specific trajectories
- postconceptional age: exposure; Postconceptional age window (36-42 weeks, early rising window; 43-46 weeks, peak/transition interval; >=47 weeks, late declining window)
- sex: stratifier; Sex of the infant (Female; Male)
- year of birth or death: stratifier; Year of birth or death (2014-2015; 2016-2017; 2018-2019; 2020-2021)
- SUID: outcome; Cause of death categorized as Sudden infant death syndrome (R95), Accidental suffocation and strangulation in bed (W75), or Other ill-defined and unspecified causes of mortality (R99)
- bed sharing: exposure; Case-level bed sharing was classified from NCFRP death-scene sleep-environment variables rather than from PRAMS. Direct evidence of same-surface sharing was retained as bed sharing.
- birthweight: stratifier; Models were stratified by low birthweight (<2,500 g).
- PCA (postconceptional age): outcome; Postconceptional age is the time elapsed since conception, measured in weeks.
- chronological age: offset; Chronological age is the time elapsed since birth, measured in weeks.
- sex (male, female): stratifier; Sex is recorded as male or female.
- birthweight (low, non-low): stratifier; Birthweight is categorized as low or non-low.
- maternal smoking status (smoking, non-smoking): stratifier; Maternal smoking is categorized as smoking or non-smoking.
- Maternal prepregnancy body mass index (BMI): exposure; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared.
- Gestational age at birth: covariate; measured in weeks.
- Maternal infections in pregnancy: exposure; chlamydia, gonorrhea and hepatitis C.
- Age of death in SUID cases: outcome; measured as days since birth.
- Geographic location: stratifier; state, latitude, and longitude.
- inner ear dysfunction: exposure; induced by intra-tympanic gentamicin (IT-Gent) injections bilaterally or unilaterally to precipitate inner ear hair cell dysfunction.
- control condition: exposure; received intra-tympanic saline (IT-Saline) bilaterally or unilaterally, or intra-peritoneal gentamicin (IP-Gent).
- body movement arousal response to severe hypoxia-hypercarbia: outcome; measured under light anesthesia 8 days following the administration of gentamicin or saline.
- hypercapnic ventilatory response: outcome; measured as part of assessing arousal responses to severe hypoxia-hypercarbia.
- age of mice: covariate; not explicitly stated, but implied to be within a timeframe suitable for the experiment.
- baseline cSN activity: outcome; measured as increased baseline sympathetic nerve activity following CIH exposure.
- breathing frequency: outcome; measured as an increase in breathing rate after chronic intermittent hypoxia.
- expiratory time: outcome; measured as a decrease in the duration of expiration following CIH exposure.
- PiCo specific cholinergic-glutamatergic neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- glutamatergic PiCo neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- ChAT containing neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- Dbx1 and Vglut2 neurons: exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- preBötzinger complex (preBötC): exposure; optogenetically stimulated to assess changes in respiratory-sympathetic coupling.
- chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH): exposure; mice exposed to chronic intermittent hypoxia for 21 days.
- diaphragm activity: outcome; measured as changes in diaphragm muscle activity.
- vagus nerve activity: outcome; measured as changes in vagal nerve activity.
- cervical sympathetic nerve activity: outcome; measured as changes in cervical sympathetic nerve activity.
- chronic intermittent hypoxia (IH): exposure; 30 days of IH exposure (IH30) in a murine model.
- adult neurogenesis: outcome; Measured by immunohistochemical experiments assessing Sox2+ neural progenitor cells, doublecortin-positive neurons, and radial glial cells in the subgranular zone.
- synaptic plasticity: outcome; Assessed by paired-pulse facilitation and long-term potentiation (LTP).
- reactive oxygen species (ROS): effect_modifier; Measured by lipid peroxidation and mitigated with antioxidant treatment.
- breathing patterns: exposure; Measured using plethysmography during the first hour after birth in mice born at term, delivered prematurely with LPS, or via C-section.
- survival: outcome; Measured as mortality rates in mice born prematurely or at term.
- inhibition: exposure; Investigated using a biophysical model and in vitro recordings from mouse pre-Bötzinger complex.
- excitation: exposure; Investigated using partial excitation block and in vitro recordings from mouse pre-Bötzinger complex.
- lipopolysaccharide (LPS): exposure; Administered intraperitoneally at 0.14 mg/kg to pregnant dams on gestational day 18.5.
- progesterone: exposure; Administered intraperitoneally at 42 mg/kg to pregnant dams on embryonic day 17.5.
- neurogenesis: outcome; Assessed by T-box transcription factor 2 (Tbr2) intermediate neural progenitor cell density and BrdU labeling.
